title: `Command(goto="__end__")` returned from tool does not stop agent loop in `create_agent`, causes invalid message order error
author: errajibadr

comments.author: KarthikeyaKollu
comments.body: @errajibadr made a PR on the same issue let me know if that works for you!!

comments.author: errajibadr
comments.body:
i'm mitigated on your solution. which is basically my Troubleshoot. 

It doesn't really respect the 
Command(goto="__end__") 

It just uses a trick based on last AI message for circuit breaker. which is not what i want nor the Expected behavior. 
Command goto should be respected whatever the last message

But i really need command to work. for other edge cases i need to implement.

comments.author: Zi-Ling
comments.body:
This feels like an execution boundary issue.

If a tool explicitly returns a terminal command,
continuing the loop seems more harmful than helpful.

Is the intention here that stop signals are best-effort,
or should they always hard-interrupt the agent loop?

comments.author: sydney-runkle
comments.body: This is expected actually - a `Command` with `goto` adds a dynamic edge, but the other static edges still execute, hence the continuation of the agent loop. You might want to use `return_direct=True` on this tool instead.

comments.author: Prudhvi0717
comments.body: @sydney-runkle `return_direct` doesn't work here. The `Command.update` added an `AIMessage` and https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/blob/main/libs/prebuilt/langgraph/prebuilt/chat_agent_executor.py#L964-L977 will return `entrypoint` -> which doesn't end the graph

comments.author: arthurdorigueto
comments.body: Maybe `AgentState`'s `"jump_to"` should be usable by tools?

comments.author: navneetgurjar
comments.body:
I think @sydney-runkle is right. @Prudhvi0717 I was able to resolve this issue in my case via: `return_direct=True.` I was also using a similar library, named `create_supervisor`, which is the previous version for creating a Supervisor....similar to `create_agent` It has similar features and issues....internally, all these are `ReAct` agents

---

When I attached some tools to it, and that tool was returning a `Command` to directly go to the end node, that wasn't happening. I visualised the graph internally. There was only one edge from the tool to the LLM (in the graph of `create_agent`. So, it only executed the internal edge instead of directly initiating the `END` node; it went to the LLM, and then the LLM used to initiate the `END` node. Following @sydney-runkle suggestion and some help from Claude Code, I set r`return_direct=True.`, tested it, and it no longer went to the LLM. After the tool was executed, it went directly to the end node. 

---

Also, one suggestion is that in your case, you are facing another issue with the LLM: that every tool call `AIMessage` must be paired with a `ToolMessage` before an LLM invocation in **OpenAI and Anthropic models as well.** This is causing an API error. To resolve this, you can add your own `ToolMessage` with the same tool invocation id or simply remove the orphaned tool call AI message before calling the LLM
